desc:
The rectangular grid holds small integers, possibly negative or zero. A route starts in the top-left cell, ends in the bottom-right cell and moves only right or down. The score of a route is the product of all values on it, including the first and the last cell.

Among all routes whose score is non-negative (zero counts), find the largest score and return it modulo 1,000,000,007. If every route has a negative score, return -1. Note that the comparison between routes uses the true product, not the remainder.
constraints: The maximum is compared exactly; only the value that is returned is reduced modulo 1,000,000,007
hints: A single best product per cell is not enough: a very negative product multiplied by a negative number becomes a very large positive one.
For every cell keep both the largest and the smallest product of a route ending there. These two numbers are enough to know every extreme that can come out of the next multiplication.

For cell value v, collect v * mx and v * mn of the cell above and of the cell to the left; the new maximum and minimum are the max and min of these four candidates. At the end, if the maximum is negative return -1, else return it modulo 1,000,000,007. Python integers will not overflow, so take the modulo only at the very end.
editorial: Multiplying by a positive value preserves order, multiplying by a negative value reverses it, and multiplying by zero collapses everything to zero. Consequently the largest product of a route into a cell can come from the largest or the smallest product of a route into one of its two predecessors, depending on the sign of the cell. Tracking mx and mn for every cell captures both possibilities.

The recurrence is: candidates = the products of the cell value with mx and mn of the upper and left cells; mx is the largest candidate and mn the smallest. The remainder must not be applied while comparing, because remainders do not preserve order; with grids of at most 40 x 40 and values up to 9 the exact products have only a few hundred bits, which big integers handle easily. If the final mx is negative every route is negative and the answer is -1, otherwise it is mx modulo 1,000,000,007. Time O(m · n), space O(n) numbers.
solution:
def maxNonNegProductRoute(grid):
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    n = len(grid[0])
    mx = [0] * n
    mn = [0] * n
    for r, row in enumerate(grid):
        for c in range(n):
            v = row[c]
            if r == 0 and c == 0:
                mx[0] = mn[0] = v
                continue
            cand = []
            if r > 0:
                cand.append(mx[c] * v)
                cand.append(mn[c] * v)
            if c > 0:
                cand.append(mx[c - 1] * v)
                cand.append(mn[c - 1] * v)
            mx[c] = max(cand)
            mn[c] = min(cand)
    return -1 if mx[-1] < 0 else mx[-1] % MOD
